correctness.rationale: The proof gives a unique powerful-core decomposition directly from prime exponents and multiplicativity of the exponential-divisor sum. Hagis’s full text was inspected for this decomposition and for the fixed-support finiteness theorem. The exact two-prime classification is explicitly recorded in the later handbook. Landau’s fixed-k almost-prime asymptotic then yields the 36-core main term; every core with at least three prime factors contributes one fewer power of log log X because there are only finitely many such cores for each fixed support size. The ratio law follows by division. A direct checker through 500000 verified every decomposition and found only 36 in the two-prime layer; the finite check is not used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A global density for the unrestricted union does not determine the count inside any fixed-omega stratum. The two-prime classification supplies the minimal core but does not dominate the claimed higher-layer asymptotics without the new counting argument.

value.rationale: Stratifying a positive-density arithmetic set by the standard invariant omega(n) is mathematically natural. The theorem explains how the global density is assembled from layers of increasing support, gives the exact scale and leading constant of every fixed layer, and identifies the unique two-prime core as the universal leading source. The consecutive-layer ratio is a structural distribution law, not an arbitrary finite slice or table recomputation.
